skill.name: mobile-design
skill.description: Provides mobile-first design guidance and a local audit workflow for accessible, performant iOS, Android, React Native, and Flutter applications.
skill.summary: Design and review mobile experiences with platform-aware interaction, performance, accessibility, navigation, backend, testing, and release guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 141 static findings are false positives caused by mobile-platform prose, Markdown backticks, placeholder URLs, regex search terms, and Dart key parameters. The local audit script reads supported source files only within the current workspace and makes no network requests or external command calls. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or other semantic security issue was found.

content.value_statement: Mobile interfaces often fail when desktop patterns ignore touch, platform behavior, accessibility, offline use, and device limits. This skill supplies focused guidance and a local source audit.
actual_capabilities: Assesses mobile feature feasibility across platform clarity, interaction complexity, performance, offline use, and accessibility.
Guides touch targets, thumb-zone placement, gestures, haptics, typography, color, navigation, and platform conventions.
Compares React Native, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose choices for stated project needs.
Reviews mobile performance, secure storage, offline behavior, API design, testing, debugging, and release readiness.
Audits React Native and Flutter source files with a local Python script using documented heuristic checks.
Reports detected issues, warnings, passed checks, and an overall compliance result.
limitations: The audit script uses regular expressions, so findings require human verification and may include false positives or missed issues.
The script checks selected JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, TSX, and Dart files, while skipping native iOS and Android directories.
Guidance does not replace real-device testing, platform documentation, security review, accessibility testing, or performance profiling.
Useful recommendations require the target platform, framework, navigation model, offline needs, device range, and audience.

use_cases.title: Review a new mobile screen
use_cases.description: Evaluate touch ergonomics, accessibility, platform conventions, loading states, error recovery, and performance before implementation.

use_cases.title: Audit a cross-platform codebase
use_cases.description: Identify heuristic React Native or Flutter issues affecting lists, gestures, storage, navigation, typography, offline behavior, and testing.

use_cases.title: Plan release readiness
use_cases.description: Create a focused validation checklist for low-end devices, accessibility, secure storage, offline handling, logging, and platform-specific behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Check one screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this [screen description] for [iOS, Android, or both]. Check touch targets, accessibility, feedback, loading, errors, and platform conventions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single mobile screen

prompt_templates.title: Improve a user flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this [user flow] built with [framework]. Recommend navigation, gesture alternatives, offline states, error recovery, and platform-specific changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit mobile source
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this [project or file set] for React Native or Flutter mobile risks. Prioritize findings by user impact and explain required validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Technical review of an existing implementation

prompt_templates.title: Design a mobile architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [feature] for [platforms] using [framework]. Include feasibility scoring, navigation, data synchronization, security, performance budgets, accessibility, tests, and release checks.

output_examples.input: Review a checkout screen for both iOS and Android.
output: Place the primary payment action within the lower thumb zone.
Use platform-native back behavior and preserve entered form data.
Provide loading, retry, offline, validation, and payment failure states.
Verify touch targets, screen-reader labels, text scaling, and contrast.

output_examples.input: Audit a React Native product list with slow scrolling.
output: Prioritize list virtualization and stable item identifiers.
Check item memoization, render callback stability, image sizing, and logging.
Profile on a low-end physical device before accepting performance changes.

output_examples.input: Plan navigation for a cross-platform account area.
output_examples.output: Use shared information architecture with platform-native back behavior, deep links, state restoration, accessible labels, and explicit authentication boundaries.

best_practices: State the target platforms, framework, devices, audience, navigation model, and offline requirements before requesting recommendations.
Validate recommendations with platform guidelines, physical devices, accessibility tools, and performance profilers.
Treat script findings as review leads, then confirm each issue in its complete source and runtime context.
anti_patterns: Do not apply one identical interaction model to iOS and Android without evaluating platform expectations.
Do not accept regex audit output as proof of correctness, security, accessibility, or production readiness.
Do not optimize appearance while ignoring touch reach, loading, recovery, offline behavior, memory, battery, and low-end devices.

faq.question: Which platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose guidance, with different depth across topics.

faq.question: Can it audit an existing mobile project?
faq.answer: Yes. The included Python script performs heuristic checks on supported React Native and Flutter source files within the current workspace.

faq.question: Does the audit script change project files?
faq.answer: No. It reads supported source files and prints issues, warnings, passed checks, and compliance status.

faq.question: Does it make network requests?
faq.answer: No. URLs appear only in documentation examples, and the script searches source text for network-related terms.

faq.question: Can it replace device testing?
faq.answer: No. Validate touch behavior, accessibility, performance, navigation, and offline recovery on representative physical devices.

faq.question: What information should a prompt include?
faq.answer: Provide platforms, framework, screen or feature goals, navigation, offline needs, device range, audience, and relevant source context.
